title: March of the Machine: The Aftermath: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: It was a time for rebuilding, but first Ikoria's wrecked cities had to be cleared of monsters.
Survivors put the strength of former war mounts to good use clearing the rubble of Orazca.
With their ancient enemy vanquished, the angels of New Capenna turned their eyes to their former captors: demons.
Phyrexia was defeated, but the repercussions of the invasion rippled through the Blind Eternities.
For those who survived, being prepared for the next crisis became one of the greatest virtues.
Conflict is a constant. Only the enemies change.
The relic shattered, and something in Nahiri broke as well.
When Nissa tapped into Zhalfir's leylines, she was shocked to feel not a piece of Dominaria, but a plane all its own.
Light shone on parts of the undercity for the first time in centuries.
"When all the stories find their ends, a new one shall begin." —*The Endsaga*
Danitha had spent her whole life preparing to lead House Capashen, but she mourned that the opportunity had come so soon.
"Our strength lies not in our walls, but in our people."
They called her unique insight a "gift." Then she saw the truth, and suddenly it was a "threat."
Stranded on New Capenna without a spark, he faced five families out for blood.
Renegade turned revolutionary turned rebuilder.
The Phyrexian design had to go, but the materials could be put to good use.
"Try to keep up, Djeru. We have lots of work to do."
"Today, we become gods again."
Like Orn before it, Drannith was reduced to a playground for Ikoria's monsters.
The glistening oil had been rendered inert, but planes wouldn't begin to truly heal until every last drop was purged.
After the invasion, many wanted to leave a life of violence. But once you're a Reckoner, you die a Reckoner.
The creature was unlike any Nissa had seen, but she dealt with it as she would any threat.
Reconstructing the past is Lorehold's specialty.
To hear them tell it, they charged bare-handed into New Phyrexia and beat up Elesh Norn all by themselves.
Worlds apart, Huatli built a device Saheeli would have been proud of.
"Zendikar is *my* home!"
The story circle continues.
